raw_response:
I've been working this land in Quzhou for most of my life. Nine mu isn't much, but it's what I manage, and at my age I know every field's behavior. My cropping system is wheat-maize on about 6 mu — that rotation has served this county well for decades — and I keep about 3 mu in cotton separately, since it still brings decent income when the price holds.

For wheat this winter, I'll use an improved variety — something like Jimai 22 or Kenong 199, proven in this soil. I'll rotary-till after the maize comes off in October, apply base fertilizer, then topdress at jointing. Four irrigations: sowing water, winter water, jointing water, heading water. That's what I've always done and the yields hold around 450 kg/mu.

Summer maize goes in immediately after wheat harvest in June — no-till, direct seeding, fast turnaround. Hybrid seed,郑单958 type. I'll water at emergence, tasseling, and grain fill. Maize doesn't need much fuss if the timing is right.

Cotton on the remaining 3 mu is more labor. I'll plough in early spring, transplant seedlings in late April. Bt hybrid to keep bollworm pressure down, but I still spray 4-5 times for aphids, mites, and other pests. Cotton is thirsty — 5 irrigations at minimum. My wife helps with topping and harvest. It's hard work but the per-mu income justifies it.

With two people and well access, this plan is manageable. I'm not experimenting at 70. I'm doing what I know works.
